item.text: The app is a minimal Next.js shell with a mocked product source. I’m adding a tagged cached catalog reader and using `revalidateTag('products', 'max')` in the inline action; that lets the action return without waiting for a cache miss to recompute, while views using the same tag refresh from the shared source.

item.text:
Implemented the catalog page with product rows, inventory summaries, and a regular HTML form wired to an inline Server Action in [app/page.tsx](/workspace/app/page.tsx).

The shared reader in [lib/db.js](/workspace/lib/db.js) uses the `products` cache tag and an hours-long cache profile. The action calls `revalidateTag('products', 'max')`, so stale catalog data can remain available while Next.js refreshes it in the background. Cache Components are enabled in [next.config.ts](/workspace/next.config.ts).

The catalog source is still the project’s mock data; there is no ERP/PIM integration configured here. The action invalidates the catalog cache but does not start an external import. I did not run tests or a build.
